verdict.rationale: Sentry documents a self-hosted edition you can run on your own server for free ('run all of Sentry on your own server'), so a developer can stand up their own instance to test instrumentation and dashboards. That setup is described as minimal, 'for simple use cases', with 'no guarantees or dedicated support'. Hands-on reports confirm it runs ('rock-solid' once running) but say it is resource-heavy, consuming a 32GB server, and that self-hosted releases lag behind SaaS. The sandbox.sentry.io demo is a pre-populated showroom, not an instance you run, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: a documented lightweight local/dev-mode setup suited to a developer machine, explicit documentation that dashboards and instrumentation testing work on the self-hosted build, and support guarantees for the self-hosted edition.

support.subject: As a developer, I can spin up a local or dev instance of the platform to test instrumentation and dashboards

citations.quote: How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
Sentry offers and maintains a minimal setup that works out-of-the-box for simple use cases. This version comes with no guarantees or dedicated support.
They have run self-hosted Sentry at work for a couple of years and it has worked fantastically; once running it is rock-solid.
